artifact: S2 post-merge gate — /api/meta git_sha tracks redeploys — RAN
why_this_exists: S2 (PR #31, merged e6810a4 2026-08-22) carried one UNRUN gate that no agent could run from inside a session: the deployed sha has to be observed MOVING across two redeploys, not merely existing (ADR-028 §g, PR #31 R9). Under ADR-022 rule 2 the row cannot archive to DONE.md while that gate is UNRUN. This file is the observation record; it makes no claim beyond the HTTP responses listed.
gate_text_verbatim: `/api/meta` reports a real sha **that tracks redeploys** — **UNRUN**, and unrunnable from here: no agent can run a Zeabur build, so this is confirmed by `curl -s https://whaleforce-sec10k.zeabur.app/api/meta` after the merge and again after a second redeploy — **the sha must MOVE across two redeploys, not merely exist**, which is the only observation that catches a cached build layer freezing a real-but-stale sha (ADR-028 §g, PR #31 R9).
how_run: Three real HTTP GETs against the deployed instance (no mocks, hard rule 4), each paired with `git log` of the commit the returned sha names. The first two were made by the orchestrator and relayed to the implementer with timestamps; the implementer could not reproduce the 1efc457 response (that build had already been replaced) and re-confirmed the current one itself.

commit_chain_since_pr31_merge.base: e6810a4 2026-08-22T09:42:29Z Merge pull request #31 from HaoweiChan/task/S2 (S2 itself; the build this gate's mechanism first shipped in)
commit_chain_since_pr31_merge.reading: Zeabur rebuilds on every push to main, so each first-parent merge after e6810a4 is a redeploy. The 07:47:22Z observation of 1efc457 proves the sha had already left e6810a4 (and 6c71ca6) for 1efc457 before this morning — move one, seen at its destination; 1efc457 -> 1ed784c between 07:47:22Z and 07:49:54Z is move two, seen at both ends. The build that was running at 07:47 was NOT the one merged 92 s earlier, so the sha was not reading from a live git checkout of main either — it changed only when the new image came up, which is the injected-at-build behaviour ADR-028 §b specifies.

verdict: RAN — SATISFIED: sha moved e6810a4 -> (6c71ca6, not observed) -> 1efc457e598d -> 1ed784ccf68e across redeploys; matches origin/main at observation (07:49:54Z and 07:51:52Z).
not_claimed: No observation of a build that FAILED to move: the cached-layer failure mode ADR-028 §g names (a real-but-stale sha frozen by a cached build layer) is excluded only by the two moves actually seen, not by any test that would force it to occur.
The 6c71ca6 (PR #33) deploy was never observed; it sits on the first-parent chain between e6810a4 and 1efc457 and is inferred from Zeabur's push-to-main trigger, not from an HTTP response.
The implementer did not reproduce the 1efc457 observation — that build was gone by 07:51; the implementer's observation confirms the current sha and the git facts only.
